advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the `chunk_by_facet` docstring to describe the balanced near-equal packing (ceil(total/n) chunks, sizes differing by <=1, each in [2,n]) instead of the stale fixed `base_chunk × size_factor` slicing.
evidence: 485:    """Pack same-``facet`` criteria into chunks of ``base_chunk × size_factor``
486:    (clamped to [2, n]). Single-turn / 2-step tier only — AGENT criteria run one
The inline comment at lines 496-500 accurately describes the new balancing, but the docstring above it (the discoverable API contract) was not updated to match.
advisory.finding: The `chunk_by_facet` docstring still describes the OLD fixed-slice behavior ('chunks of `base_chunk × size_factor` (clamped to [2, n])'), but the implementation now produces near-equal balanced chunks (sizes total//k and total//k+1), so the docstring misdescribes what the function does.
advisory.suggested_fix: Revise lines 485-487 to state that criteria are packed into ceil(total/n) contiguous near-equal chunks (each within [2, n] for total>=2), rather than fixed base_chunk×size_factor slices.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit count==1 case asserting the documented single-chunk behavior for chunk_by_facet.
evidence: registry.py:498-499 docstring: 'For total >= 2 every chunk is guaranteed within [2, n]' — the guarantee explicitly excludes total==1, but no test pins what total==1 actually returns
advisory.finding: The regression test asserts every chunk is within [2, 6] for counts 2..39, but never covers count == 1 — the documented boundary where balanced packing CANNOT avoid a singleton chunk (k=1, base=1 → one 1-element chunk). The lower boundary of the [2,n] guarantee is untested, so a regression that lets count==1 (or the k arithmetic) misbehave is not caught.
scenarios: A single-criterion facet set (or single canonical criterion) hits count==1; the behavior there is asserted nowhere.
